n: This is Alex, an Aussie secret agent whose idea of deep cover involves a dodgy lanyard and a very squeaky rubber chicken.
He’s infiltrating India's biggest scam syndicate as 'Gary Windows', a tech support guru who’s about to cause a system crash.
His first masterstroke is breezing past security by guessing the central server password, which is of course, Password one two three.
But he’s not alone, because a rogue pigeon has just invaded the terminal and is now playing Minesweeper as the ultimate diversion.
When cornered by a suspicious manager, Alex deploys his secret weapon, claiming the rubber chicken is next-generation anti-hacking security hardware.
The chaos escalates when his feathered accomplice accidentally trips the fire alarm, triggering a beautiful symphony of spilling chai and panicked scammers.
Safely back in his questionable hotel room, he transfers all the syndicate's dirt onto a ridiculously fluffy pink cat USB drive.
He needs backup, so he recruits the Grey Avengers, a ruthless squad of pensioners armed with righteous fury and very overripe tomatoes.
The raid begins with a fruity fiasco, as a pensioner accidentally snipes a police inspector directly in the face with a squishy projectile.
Just as the chaos hits its peak, an old dear pulls the fire alarm seconds before a massive explosion rocks the villain’s hideout.
To establish dominance, their eighty-year-old enforcer promptly smashes an expensive sculpture, claiming he’s simply correcting the sanctuary’s negative juju flow.
They stage a completely phony exorcism, convincing the paranoid cult leader to surrender his diamond-encrusted pen to be used as ghost bait.
With a puff of freezing mist and some dramatic chanting, they triumphantly seal the imaginary financial demon inside a slightly dented thermos.
Back in Kolkata, Alex strikes gold, unearthing hilarious security footage of the syndicate's big boss trying to socially engineer a pop-up toaster.
Armed with the world's most pathetic blackmail material, he convinces Interpol to fly his entire squad of senior citizens straight to India.
Their nearly-blind getaway driver confidently rolls their clunky florist van straight through the main gates of the syndicate’s fortified headquarters.
These aren't just pensioners, they're a finely-tuned machine of chaos, ready to serve justice one overripe vegetable at a time, mate.
Covered in a glorious mess of tomato pulp, Alex watches his smug pigeon co-pilot pull a victory barrel-roll above the mayhem.
When the news crews arrive looking for a hero, Alex just deadpans the words 'rubber chicken' straight into the microphone.
The entire street spontaneously erupts into a wild Bollywood dance party, complete with cartwheeling retirees tumbling gracefully into decorative ferns.
Amid the beautiful crimson aftermath, a proud vigilante officially adopts a single pristine souvenir fruit, affectionately naming the tomato 'Terry'.
Back at the hotel, the relentless pigeon struts into Alex's room with the undeniable swagger of a tiny, feathered crime lord.
He reunites with his legendary hacker mate Juzzie, and they use a stolen toilet-paper complaint login to launch a global cyber-strike.
From a single laptop, they begin dismantling the entire criminal network, causing financial chaos for scammers from Mumbai to Mozambique.
Touching down in Brisbane, border security immediately recognizes the world-famous celebrity pigeon now perched triumphantly on our hero's shoulder.
But his homecoming is cut short by an ambush from his own team, as the Grey Avengers welcome him with a ceremonial tomato.
The celebration moves to the Redcliffe Community Hall, where the bingo machine has been temporarily repurposed for a much more important mission.
In front of a cheering crowd, Alex absolutely obliterates a cardboard effigy of the scam boss with one perfectly lethal tomato throw.
They are the heroes we didn't know we needed, proving that age is no barrier to delivering some good old-fashioned fruity justice.
They started a fire that can't be put out, a revolution built on mayhem, madness, and a whole lot of glorious mess.
With Juzzie on the keys and Alex on the ground, no dodgy call center or fake invoice is safe from their unique brand of chaos.
This summer, get ready for a tidal wave of tomato-fueled takedowns that will leave you breathless from laughing so hard, mate.
He’s got a plan for every problem, and a bird for every computer system that desperately needs a good game of Minesweeper.
Get ready to join the party, because when these legends fight back, the victory celebration is an absolutely mandatory Bollywood dance number.
He's got the world's most famous pigeon, a knack for trouble, and a complete disregard for international diplomatic protocols.
He came back a hero, welcomed by the only people who truly understand his methods: a squad of fruit-wielding, fearless pensioners.
He’s got a license to thrill, a rubber chicken for protection, and a very, very particular set of ridiculous skills.
He is Gary Windows, and he's here to scam the scammers... Juzzy Style. You have got to be kidding me, mate.
